topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the scope of the cancer lecture series, and the specific learning objectives regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Concepts of Cancer Causation and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-factorial nature of cancer development, weighing intrinsic biological errors and genetic predisposition against environmental exposures and population-level epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how viral and bacterial pathogens contribute to malignancy, illustrated through the etiology and chromosomal translocation mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Molecular Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how environmental chemicals, dietary toxins, and radiation undergo metabolic processing to form DNA adducts and genetic mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and the Multi-Stage Model of Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics differentiate tumor initiators from promoters by examining how non-mutagenic stimuli like chronic inflammation and signaling agonists drive the clonal expansion of mutated cells.

topics.label: Host Susceptibility Factors and Carcinogenesis Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tissue development and life stages influence vulnerability to malignant transformation, followed by a synthesis of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine whether specific agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Risk Analysis and Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by reviewing the everyday trade-offs between carcinogenic risks and practical benefits alongside final concluding remarks.
